blocks.text: Pink Princess is an aesthetic that empathizes girlish innocence, elegance, compassion, and living a life of pleasure and luxury. Although it burrows elements from different time periods, the aesthetic mostly uses imagery inspired by the Rococo era due to Marie Antionette and the era's fashion and lifestyle being used for inspiration. It can be considered a sub-aesthetic to Princesscore, as they are both visually and thematically similar. However, while Princesscore is about the fantasy of being a royal princess, Pink Princess is more centered around upper-class life.

Visually, the style is very similar to Romantic Academia, although it is not an academic aesthetic. Pink Parisian also has a significant influence on Pink Princess. The color palette is heavy on pink tones combined with gold, white, or cream, with other pastel colors being slightly less common. Silver is sometimes used, but is much less common than gold.

Pink Princess aesthetic embodies the philosophy of "Take your pleasure seriously" a phrase widely spread on Tumblr after user laduree-et-cigarettes answered an ask about it. Self love and treating oneself, especially in the form of luxuriating in the bathtub and sleeping, are a large part of this philosophy.

Additionally, the Pink Princess aesthetic encourages kindness, generosity, and compassion, despite being a wealth-related aesthetic. Many bloggers emphasize that their content is not meant for homophobes, transphobes, or racists.
1950s-1960s era clothing as well as 17/18th century style costumes
Baby animals like bunnies, lambs, and kittens
Gold and silver cutlery with ornate handles
Hair bows/ribbons (including on fluffy cats and small dogs)
Silver or gold dressing table sets (mirror, hairbrush, comb, nail file, vanities, etc)
Luxurious baths with flower petals, candles, champagne, etc

Clothing is ultra-feminine and made in soft fabrics like silk, satin, cotton, cashmere, and high quality wool. It is often embellished with ruffles, bows, and lace. The color black is usually limited to shoes, if worn at all. Although Rococo influence is a huge part of the Pink Princess Aesthetic, in fashion, Marie-Antoinette style outfits are usually only used for costumes and fashion is instead mainly inspired by 20th century vintage looks especially inspired by French It Girl/French Chic fashion except more girly.
Silk or satin nightgowns, pajama sets and/or dressing gowns in solid pink and other pastel colors or striped patterns in pastels
White cotton or flannel nightgowns with lace
Lady Dior bags in pink and similar girly purses (sometimes with small dogs inside)
Flower Knows (especially the Strawberry Cupid and Strawberry Rococo collections)

Men take a backseat in the lives of the Pink Princess. Often the man behind the camera for bloggers; when a boyfriend does appear, his clothing compliments hers but doesn't overshadow it. The dynamic is very Ken and Barbie.
Always clean shaven with groomed eyebrows
Hair is styled, but casual Might have a slight quiff or parted and slicked back but not heavily gelled
Suits (influenced by early 1960s men's fashion, but tailored to the body instead of having wide shoulders and baggy trousers)
Casual wear (khaki shorts, dark wash jeans, fitted t-shirts in solid colors or stripes)
